questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}-(-1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of an Exponential Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{0}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={e}^{x}\,{|}_{-5}^{0} \\  & ={e}^{0}-{e}^{-5} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{e}^{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-(-\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =-1-(-\sqrt{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}-1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6}{csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡x{|}_{\pi /2}^{5\pi /6} \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6})-(-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =-(-\sqrt{3})-0 \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{5}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={e}^{x}\,{|}_{2}^{5} \\  & ={e}^{5}-{e}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{5}-{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
